info.title: Social Network for Fellow Servicemen — API
info.description:
The goal of the work is to develop a social network for former fellow
servicemen: simplified search and communication for those who served in
the same unit.

# Functional requirements
- Creating and editing your profile
- Posting entries on your profile
- Searching, adding, and removing friends
- Communicating with friends in chat
- Searching, subscribing to, and unsubscribing from groups
- Ability to leave comments on group and user posts

# Scope of this document (milestones 1-5)
REST surface: accounts (email/password), user profiles, friends,
subscriptions, groups, pastes (posts), comments, chats and media
upload/fetch. Realtime chat delivery is a WebSocket channel documented
separately in asyncapi.yaml (the REST write path POST
/chats/{ChatID}/messages is what triggers the realtime push).

# Authentication
Sign up, then sign in to receive a JWT access token. Send it on every
request except `/account/signup` and `/account/signin`:

    Authorization: Bearer <token>

Token claims: `sub` — user identifier (string), `exp` — Unix expiration
time, `role` — `user` or `admin`. Default lifetime is 3600 seconds.
Admins are fixed accounts (emails listed server-side in `admins.json`);
they get the `admin` role at signup.

On 401 the body is `{"detail": "..."}` with one of exactly three values:
`"Not authenticated"` (no/unknown scheme header), `"Invalid token"`,
`"Token expired"`. Use them to decide between redirecting to sign-in and
silently refreshing/re-authenticating.

# Personal groups
On signup the backend automatically creates a *personal group* linked to
the user (a feed for their personal posts). Personal groups surface in
subscription lists as `sub_type: "user"` entries (see
`SubscriptionListItem`); topic groups created by admins surface as
`sub_type: "group"`.

# Pagination
Collections accept `limit` (1–100, default 10) and `offset` (number of
items skipped, default 0) and return plain arrays ordered by id.

# Errors
All errors return `{"detail": ...}` (see `Error`). For malformed requests
(bad JSON, failed field validation — including wrong query-parameter
ranges) the backend answers **400** with `detail` as an array of
validation error objects, not FastAPI's default 422.

# Changes versus draft v0.3
1. `POST /users/{UserID}/friends` body is `FriendPost` (v0.3 referenced a
   non-existent `Friend` schema); content type is `application/json`.
2. `POST /users/{UserID}/subscriptions` body is `SubscriptionPost`
   (v0.3 referenced a non-existent `Subscription` schema).
3. `POST /account/signup` body is `SignUpRequest` (v0.3 referenced a
   non-existent `SignUpRequest` schema).
4. `SubscriptionListItem` gained a required `id` field — otherwise
   `DELETE /users/{UserID}/subscriptions/{SubscriptionID}` could not be
   used from the list response.
5. Token payload additionally carries `role` (`user`/`admin`) so clients
   can render admin-only UI; the backend remains the source of truth.
6. `photo_url` may be an empty string while the media endpoint does not
   exist yet.
7. `POST /groups/{GroupID}/pastes` body is `PastePost` (`{text}` only) —
   v0.3 referenced a `PastePost` schema that was not defined in
   components; the group comes from the path and the author from the
   token.
8. Commenting body is `CommentPost` (`{text}` only) — v0.3 referenced the
   full `Comment` schema, whose `id`, `time` and `author` are
   server-generated.
9. `Paste` intentionally keeps its v0.3 shape (no author field); the
   backend tracks the author internally for permission checks. If feeds
   need to show the post author, add `author: UserListItem` (as `Comment`
   already has) in a future revision.
10. `Message` responses expose `user_id` (the author) — v0.3's property
    list said `chat_member_id` while its required list said `user_id`;
    `user_id` won. The message POST body is `MessagePost` (`{text}` only),
    since v0.3 referenced the full `Message` schema whose id/author/time
    are server-generated.
11. `ChatPost.name` and `ChatPost.photo_url` are optional — a personal
    1:1 chat has no client-supplied name (it is rendered for each
    participant from the other participant's profile).
12. Chat membership rules the spec leaves open: creating a personal chat
    is idempotent (a second create for the same pair returns the existing
    chat); personal chats are fixed (adding/removing members is 403); in
    public chats any member may add users (the body's `is_owner` is
    ignored — ownership is assigned at creation), a member may leave, the
    owner may remove anyone except themself and cannot be removed.
    Unknown users in chat bodies answer 404.
13. `POST /media` takes a proper multipart body with a `file` field
    (v0.3 declared `type: binary` directly under multipart/form-data,
    which is not a valid multipart schema). Only images are accepted
    (image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp); the size limit is
    5 MB by default. A `GET /media/{MediaID}` endpoint was added (it
    does not exist in v0.3) so the returned `photo_url` resolves; it is
    public on purpose. Attach the returned URL to a profile or a group
    via the `photo_url` field of the respective PATCH body.

host.description: Base host; a reverse proxy may add the /api/v1 prefix transparently

tags.name: account
tags.description: Registration and sign-in. No token required.

tags.name: users
tags.description: User profiles, search, friends and subscriptions. All operations require a bearer token.

tags.name: groups
tags.description: Topic groups (created by admins), personal-post feeds, their pastes (posts) and comments. All operations require a bearer token.

tags.name: chats
tags.description: Personal (1:1) and public chats, their members and messages (REST polling; realtime delivery is a separate AsyncAPI/WebSocket concern). All operations require a bearer token.

tags.name: media
tags.description: Image upload (avatars, group photos) and fetch. Uploading requires a bearer token; fetching stored files is public so photo URLs work inside tags.

post.description:
Creates the account, the user's personal group and the user profile
in one step. The password is stored as a bcrypt hash.
No token required. A successful response has an empty body.

Validates the credentials and returns a JWT access token.
Admins sign in here too (their token carries `role: "admin"`).
No token required.

200.description: Signed in; the body is the raw JWT string.

get.description:
Lists users, optionally filtered. Both filters are case-insensitive
substring matches and combine with AND. Results are ordered by id.

404.description: Such a user does not exist.

patch.description:
Only the profile owner may edit (the token's `sub` must equal
`UserID`; even admins are rejected). Merge-patch semantics: provide
only the fields to change; JSON `null` is treated the same as an
absent field. The response has an empty body.

delete.description:
Removes the user from the social network. Requires the `admin` role.
Cascades: the account, the personal group, the user's friendships and
subscriptions are removed too. The deleted user can no longer sign in.

get.description:
Friends of `UserID`, visible to any authenticated user. The optional
name/surname filters work as in `GET /users`.

post.description:
Adds `user_id` (from the body) as a friend of `UserID`. Only the
owner of the friends list may call this (`sub` must equal `UserID`).
Friendship is symmetric: it appears in both users' lists.

400.description:
Malformed body, `user_id` equals `UserID`
("Cannot add yourself as a friend"), or the users are already
friends ("Users are already friends").

404.description: The caller or the target user does not exist.

delete.description:
Removes `FriendID` from `UserID`'s friends (symmetric). Only the
owner of the list may call this.

get.description:
Groups `UserID` is subscribed to. Subscriptions to personal groups
are rendered as user entries (see `SubscriptionListItem.sub_type`).

400.description: Malformed body, or already subscribed ("Already subscribed to this group").

403.description:
Caller is not the subscriber and not an admin, tried to set
`is_moderator` without the admin role, or tried to set
`is_moderator` on a personal group.

404.description: The user or the group does not exist.

delete.description:
Removes subscription `SubscriptionID` (its value comes from the `id`
field of `SubscriptionListItem`). A regular user may only remove
their own subscriptions; an admin may remove anyone's.

404.description: Such a subscription does not exist.

get.description:
Lists topic groups, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive
substring of the name. Results are ordered by id. Personal groups
(user post feeds) are **not** listed here — they are discovered
through users and subscriptions.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the group name.

post.description:
Creates a new topic group. Requires the `admin` role. The id is
server-assigned. A successful response has an empty body; fetch the
created group via `GET /groups/{GroupID}`.

get.description:
Works for topic groups and for personal groups (a user's post feed;
its `name` is the owner's email set at signup).

patch.description:
Requires the `admin` role; even a moderator of the group is rejected.
Merge-patch semantics: provide only the fields to change; JSON `null`
is treated the same as an absent field. The response has an empty body.

delete.description:
Requires the `admin` role. Cascades: the group's pastes, all comments
on them and every subscription to the group are removed too.

200.description: A page of pastes ordered by id.

post.summary: Publish a post in the group
post.description:
Who may publish:
- in a **personal** group — only its owner (posting on your profile);
- in a **topic** group — the admin and the group's moderators
  (subscribers with `is_moderator: true`).
The author is taken from the token. A successful response has an
empty body; fetch the paste via the list or `GET .../pastes/{PasteID}`.

403.description: Caller may not publish in this group.

get.description: A paste addressed under a group it does not belong to is 404.

delete.description:
Allowed for the admin, the group's moderator (topic groups), or the
owner of the personal group. Cascades: the post's comments are
removed too.

403.description: Caller may not delete this post.

200.description: A page of comments ordered by id.

post.description:
Any authenticated user may comment. The author is taken from the
token. A successful response has an empty body; fetch comments via
the list above.

get.description:
The "My messages" tab: chats the caller is a member of, ordered by id.
A personal chat is listed under the **other** participant's name and
photo (like in messengers); a public chat under its own name.

post.description:
`chat_type: "personal"` — a fixed 1:1 chat with the single user from
`users` (the caller is added automatically). Creation is idempotent:
a second create for the same pair (from either side) returns the
existing chat instead of duplicating it.

`chat_type: "public"` — a group chat named `name`; the caller becomes
its owner, `users` are the initial members.

A successful response has an empty body; find the chat id via
`GET /chats`.

400.description:
Malformed body, or a personal chat whose `users` is not exactly
one other user ("A personal chat requires exactly one other user").

404.description: A user from `users` does not exist.

get.description: Members only. Ordered by user id.

200.description: A page of members with their owner flags.

post.summary: Add a user to the chat
post.description:
Members only. Allowed only in public chats (personal chats are fixed,
403). The body's `is_owner` is accepted for compatibility but ignored:
ownership is assigned at chat creation only. Adding an existing member
is 400; an unknown user is 404.

200.description: User added to the chat (empty body).

400.description: Malformed body, or the user is already a member ("User is already a chat member").

403.description: Caller is not a member, or the chat is personal.

404.description: The chat or the target user does not exist.

delete.summary: Remove a user from the chat
delete.description:
A member may remove themself (leave); the chat owner may remove
anyone except themself. The owner cannot be removed by anyone and
cannot leave (403). Personal chats are fixed (403).

200.description: User removed from the chat (empty body).

403.description: Caller lacks the rights, or the chat is personal, or the target is the owner.

404.description: The chat or the membership does not exist.

get.description: Members only. Ordered by id (oldest first).

post.summary: Send a message to the chat
post.description:
Members only. The author and time are taken from the token and the
server clock. A successful response has an empty body; read the
messages back via `GET /chats/{ChatID}/messages`.

403.description: Caller is not a chat member.

post.description:
Accepts multipart/form-data with a single `file` field. Only images
are accepted: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`.
An empty file or a file above the size limit (5 MB by default) is
rejected with 400. The response carries `photo_url` — attach it to a
profile or a group via the `photo_url` field of the respective PATCH
body. External image URLs are also allowed in PATCH bodies; media
upload is simply the way to host images on this server.

400.description:
Missing `file` field, empty file, unsupported content type
("Unsupported media type; allowed: image/png, image/jpeg,
image/gif, image/webp") or file too large ("File is too large").

get.description: Returns the stored bytes with their original content type. This endpoint is intentionally public (no bearer token): photo URLs must be usable inside `` tags, and profile/group photos are public data in this API.

bearerAuth.description:
JWT issued by `POST /account/signin`. Claims:
- `sub` — user identifier (string of digits)
- `exp` — Unix expiration time (default TTL 3600 s)
- `role` — `user` or `admin`

FriendID.name: FriendID
FriendID.description: Identifier of the friend to remove.

GroupID.name: GroupID
GroupID.description: Identifier of the group (topic group or personal group).

MemberID.name: MemberID
MemberID.description: Identifier of the chat member to remove (a user id).

MediaID.name: MediaID
MediaID.description: Identifier of the stored media file.

NameQuery.name: name
NameQuery.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the first name.

SurnameQuery.name: surname
SurnameQuery.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the last name.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

BadRequest.description:
Invalid data: malformed JSON body, failed field validation (including
query-parameter ranges) or a business-rule rejection. `detail` is a
string for business rules and an array of validation error objects
for request-validation failures.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, malformed or expired bearer token. `detail` is exactly one
of "Not authenticated", "Invalid token", "Token expired".

Forbidden.description: The token is valid but the caller lacks the required rights.

NotFound.description: The requested entity does not exist.

UserListItem.description: Short user form used in search results.

personal_group_id.description: id of the personal group created together with the user.

photo_url.description: May be an empty string until media upload exists.

User.description: Full user profile returned by GET /users/{UserID}.

examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

photo_url.description: May be an empty string until media upload exists.

UserPatch.description: Editable profile fields. All optional; omitted fields (and JSON null) are left unchanged.

examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

user_id.description: The user to add as a friend.

is_moderator.description: May be requested only by an admin and only for topic groups. Silently rejected otherwise (403).

SubscriptionListItem.description: One subscription row. For a topic group: `sub_type` is "group", `user_id` is -1 and `name`/`photo_url` come from the group. For a personal group (a user's personal-post feed): `sub_type` is "user", `user_id` is the owner's id, and `name`/`photo_url` come from the owner's profile.

id.description: Subscription identifier; use it to unsubscribe.

group_id.description: The subscribed group (also when sub_type is "user").

user_id.description: -1 for topic groups; the profile owner's id for user feeds.

name.description: Group name, or "FirstName LastName" for user feeds.
examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

GroupListItem.description: Short group form used in search results (topic groups only).

examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

photo_url.description: May be an empty string until media upload exists.

GroupPost.description: Body of POST /groups; the id is server-assigned.

examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

Group.description: Full group profile returned by GET /groups/{GroupID}.

name.description: For personal groups this is the owner's email (set at signup); for topic groups the name given at creation.
examples: 209th Separate Railway Brigade of the Orders of Kutuzov 2nd Degree and the Red Star

photo_url.description: May be an empty string until media upload exists.

GroupPatch.description: Editable group fields (admin only). All optional; omitted fields (and JSON null) are left unchanged.

PastePost.description: Body of POST /groups/{GroupID}/pastes. The group comes from the path and the author from the token, so only the text is accepted.

Paste.description: A post in a group. Kept in the v0.3 shape: it has no author field (the backend tracks the author internally for permission checks).

CommentPost.description: Body of the comment POST. The paste comes from the path and the author from the token; `id` and `time` are server-generated.

Comment.description: A comment on a paste, with the author's short profile.

ChatPost.description: Body of POST /chats. `name` and `photo_url` are optional (a personal chat is named after the other participant). `users` holds the *other* participants; the caller is always added automatically.

users.description: Exactly one user for a personal chat; any list for a public chat.

ChatListItem.description: Short chat form for the chat list. For a personal chat the name and photo are the *other* participant's, per viewer.

photo_url.description: May be an empty string until media upload exists.

Chat.description: Full chat profile returned by GET /chats/{ChatID}.

ChatMemberPost.description: Body of POST /chats/{ChatID}/members. `is_owner` is accepted for compatibility with v0.3 but ignored (ownership is assigned at chat creation only).

user_id.description: The user to add to the chat.

ChatMemberListItem.description: One chat membership with the member's short profile.

is_owner.description: True only for the public chat's creator.

MessagePost.description: Body of the message POST. The chat comes from the path, the author from the token, the time from the server clock.

Message.description: One chat message; `user_id` is the author.

file.description: The image file. Allowed content types: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp. Maximum size 5 MB by default (server-configurable).

photo_url.description: Path of the stored file, e.g. "/media/42". Resolve it against the API host (a reverse proxy may make it absolute). Attach it to a profile or a group via the `photo_url` field of the respective PATCH body.

detail.description:
Human-readable message, e.g. "User does not have access rights".
For 400 request-validation failures this is instead an array of
validation error objects (FastAPI/Pydantic format).

loc.description: Path to the offending value, e.g. ["body", "password"].

examples: String should have at least 6 characters
